value.text: Our strategy is to deliver insights and experiences that make us essential to the investor workflow.

strategic_priorities.quote:
Our strategy is to deliver insights and experiences that make us essential to the investor workflow.
We are currently focused on the following five strategic priorities:

value.text: Win for Investors: Deliver differentiated insights and solutions that make us essential to investors by emphasizing research as the company's research & development (R&D) engine.

strategic_priorities.quote: • Win for Investors: Deliver diff erentiated insights and solutions that make us essential to investors by emphasizing research as the company’s research & development (R&D) engine.

value.text: Lead in AI to Empower Investor Success: Make Morningstar AI-native, rethinking capabilities and processes to greatly improve the speed and quality of insights and experiences essential to the investor workflow.

strategic_priorities.quote: • Lead in AI to Empower Investor Success: Make Morningstar AI-native, rethinking capabilities and processes to greatly improve the speed and quality of insights and experiences essential to the investor workflow.

value.text: Own the Language of Markets: Become the trusted universal language for public and private markets.

strategic_priorities.quote: • Own the Language of Markets: Become the trusted universal language for public and private markets.

value.text: Scale for Impact: Drive operational excellence and scalability to support profitable growth.

strategic_priorities.quote: • Scale for Impact: Drive operational excellence and scalability to support profitable growth.

value.text: Build an Exceptional Culture: Foster a workplace where every employee is empowered to make a difference and act with integrity.

strategic_priorities.quote: • Build an Exceptional Culture: Foster a workplace where every employee is empowered to make a difference and act with integrity.

value.text: A key aspect of our growth strategy is to expand and enhance our existing products and services, striving to adopt new technology, including AI.

strategic_priorities.quote: A key aspect of our growth strategy is to expand and enhance our existing products and services. We strive to adopt new technology, including AI, that can improve our products and services.

value.text: Sharpen Morningstar Sustainalytics' focus on its core data, research and ratings businesses by retiring the second-party opinions product

strategic_priorities.quote: In January 2026, we announced our plans to retire our second-party opinions product by the end of the first quarter as part of a broader effort to sharpen Morningstar Sustainalytics’ focus on its core data, research and ratings businesses.

value.text: Delivering insights across asset classes to public and private market investors — making Morningstar the common language of public and private markets

strategic_priorities.quote: Company Goal One Delivering insights across asset classes to public and private market investors One of our highest-priority initiatives is to make Morningstar the common language of public and private markets.

value.text: Leveraging advances in artificial intelligence to drive innovation across internal and external products and services

strategic_priorities.quote: Leveraging advances in artificial intelligence to drive innovation across internal and external products and services We introduced a dedicated AI goal in 2025 and made significant progress during the year in three primary areas.

value.text: Driving operational excellence and scalability to support growth targets

strategic_priorities.quote: Driving operational excellence and scalability to support growth targets We made important progress in companywide initiatives as well as segment-specific projects to drive scale across the business and support future growth.

value.text: Building an amazing culture that supports exceptional talent

strategic_priorities.quote: Building an amazing culture that supports exceptional talent In an AI world, where human-in-the-loop efforts are key to our competitive edge, our people—10,973 permanent, full-time employees globally as of as of Dec. 31, 2025—remain one of our most important assets.

value.text: Increasing adjusted operating income and margins

strategic_priorities.quote: We remain focused on increasing adjusted operating income and margins.

value.text: Continuing to invest in Morningstar Credit through cycles, focusing on the longer-term growth trendline and more balanced capabilities

strategic_priorities.quote: We plan to keep investing in this area, acknowledging that credit rating activity can vary widely from year to year. We remain focused on the longer-term growth trendline as we develop a more balanced set of capabilities that extend beyond our traditional areas of strength.

value.text: Focusing Morningstar Wealth on core Investment Management and Morningstar Investor after streamlining

strategic_priorities.quote: Morningstar Wealth is now focused on its core Investment Management business, which includes Morningstar Model Portfolios and the International Wealth Platform, and Morningstar Investor, which serves the individual market.

value.text: Scaling Morningstar Indexes via the CRSP acquisition

strategic_priorities.quote: We expect this acquisition to be a game changer in our efforts to scale up Morningstar Indexes.

value.text: Prioritizing a strong balance sheet for flexibility while returning capital via dividends and buybacks

strategic_priorities.quote: We continue to prioritize a strong balance sheet to provide flexibility.

value.name: Morningstar Direct Platform
value.note: In 2025, the composition of the key product areas within the segment was updated; the document states there were no changes to the overall composition of the segment.

segments.quote: In 2025, we updated the composition of the key product areas (Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, Morningstar Advisor Workstation) within the Morningstar Direct Platform segment. There were no changes to the overall composition of the Morningstar Direct Platform segment.
We operate our business through five reportable segments: Morningstar Direct Platform, PitchBook, Morningstar Credit, Morningstar Wealth, and Morningstar Retirement.

Morningstar Credit provides investors with credit ratings, research, data, and credit analytics solutions that, we believe, contribute to the transparency of international and domestic credit markets. Morningstar Credit includes Morningstar DBRS and Morningstar Credit Analytics (MCA).

value.name: Morningstar Wealth
value.note: Document states plans announced in February 2025 to retire Morningstar Office, and completion in 2025 of the retirement of the US Morningstar Wealth Turnkey Asset Management Platform (TAMP).

segments.quote: In February 2025, we announced plans to retire Morningstar Office, our practice and portfolio management software for registered investment advisors (RIAs). The transition of clients to SS&C's Black Diamond and alternative platforms is underway and is expected to be completed in early 2026. In 2025, we also completed the retirement of our US Morningstar Wealth Turnkey Asset Management Platform (TAMP) following the sale of customer assets to AssetMark in 2024.
Morningstar Retirement’s primary offerings include managed retirement accounts (MRA), fiduciary services, and custom models.

value.description: Entry into new multi-currency Credit Agreement with Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent providing borrowing capacity of up to $1.5 billion: a five-year $750.0 million revolving credit facility, a five-year delayed draw term facility of up to $375.0 million (A-1) and a three-year $375.0 million term facility (A-2).

events.quote: The Credit Agreement provides Morningstar with a multi-currency credit facility with a borrowing capacity of up to $1.5 billion, including a five-year $750.0 million revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”), a five-year delayed draw term facility of up to $375.0 million (the “A-1 Facility”) and a three-year $375.0 million term facility (the “A-2 Facility” and, together with the A-1 Facility and the Revolving Credit Facility, the “Facility”).

value.description: Termination of the existing credit agreement dated May 6, 2022 in connection with entry into the new Credit Agreement; $170.0 million outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility as of October 31, 2025 representing a rollover of prior amounts.

events.quote: In connection with the entry into the Credit Agreement, the Company terminated its existing credit agreement, dated as of May 6, 2022, among the Company, certain subsidiaries of the Company, Bank of America, N.A. and the other lenders party thereto (as amended, restated or supplemented from time to time, the "Existing Credit Agreement"). As of October 31, 2025, the aggregate principal balance outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility was $170.0 million, which represents a rollover of amounts outstanding under the Company’s previous credit agreement.

value.description: Covenants under the new Facility include a Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio not greater than 3.50 to 1.00 (4.00 to 1.00 following a Material Acquisition) and a Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio not less than 3.00 to 1.00, plus restrictions on paying dividends.

events.quote: These include, among others, that (i) the Company shall have a Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio as of the end of any fiscal quarter of the Company of not greater than 3.50 to 1.00; provided that, solely with respect to the four fiscal quarters following any Material Acquisition (as defined in the Credit Agreement), the Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio determined as of the end of such four fiscal quarters shall not be greater than 4.00 to 1.00 (ii) the Company shall have a Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio as of the end of any fiscal quarter of not less than 3.00 to 1.00.

value.why_notable: Recurring, distinctive statement of Morningstar's refusal to give guidance, framed as a governance choice.

notable_language.quote: We do not make public financial forecasts for our business because we want to avoid creating any incentives for our management team to make speculative statements about our financial results that could influence our stock price or take actions that help us meet short-term forecasts, but may not build long-term shareholder value.

value.why_notable: Unusually direct acknowledgment of political risk to the ESG business, a shift in emphasis from ESG as pure opportunity.

notable_language.quote: The politicization of ESG-related business activities and investments has increased in recent years, particularly in the US. This politicization may result in Morningstar facing heightened scrutiny in this regard, and may result in the company incurring increased costs in addressing related inquiries.

value.why_notable: Explicit naming of the sitting administration and SEC leadership churn as a business risk — a new and pointed framing.

notable_language.quote: Additionally, current regulatory uncertainty in the US — including changes and the pace of changes enacted by the current presidential administration and related leadership changes at US government agencies such as the US Securities and Exchange Commission, as well as recent and potential future US Supreme Court rulings — may impact our business.

value.why_notable: Frames a declining ESG business as a deliberate business-model transition rather than demand loss; 'softness' is a hedge.

notable_language.quote: Morningstar Sustainalytics revenue decreased $5.3 million or 4.5%. Organic revenue decreased 7.1%, largely driven by the continued streamlining of the licensed-ratings offering as the company transitions to a model focused on licensing the use and distribution of existing ratings and underlying data, as well as softness in second-party opinions.

value.why_notable: Direct admission of flat user growth and churn in the company's fastest-growing franchise.

notable_language.quote: This was partially offset by continued softness in the corporate client segment, especially with smaller firms with more limited use cases. PitchBook licensed users were relatively flat compared to the prior-year period, reflecting the addition of new logos offset by churn.

value.why_notable: Self-congratulatory summary claim placed at the end of an extended list of regulatory and macro risks.

notable_language.quote: Overall, our business, balance sheet, technological infrastructure, and teams have shown resilience and flexibility navigating global macroeconomic trends.

value.why_notable: Admission that a previously disclosed retention metric could not be produced — a withdrawal of a metric investors track.

notable_language.quote: In addition, the revenue renewal rate for Morningstar Advisor Workstation was not available in 2025 due to ongoing updates to our billing system and a product transition.

value.why_notable: Explicit disclosure of downward discretion, with the CEO himself recommending the reduction — an unusually specific and self-critical rationale for overriding a formulaic 115.5% funding.

notable_language.quote: However, due to a few delayed product deliveries, our CEO recommended and the Compensation Committee approved the application of negative discretion to reduce the 2025 annual incentive payout to 111.4% of target.

value.why_notable: Frames the removal of the 60% funding floor as a voluntary enhancement rather than a response to shareholder pressure.

notable_language.quote: Given the significant shareholder support, the Compensation Committee did not make changes to the Company’s executive compensation program in response to the 2025 say on pay vote, but did make one enhancement to the 2025 program intended to further align pay and performance by removing the funding floor from the 2025 annual incentive funding formula, as described further below.

value.why_notable: Documents a concrete structural tightening of the bonus plan and the stated justification for it.

notable_language.quote: Beginning with the 2025 annual incentive program, the Compensation Committee removed the 60% funding floor used in 2024 (and prior years) with the intention to further align with market practices and enhance alignment of pay and performance.

value.why_notable: Committee justifies awards that carry zero reported grant-date value, meaning a large potential pay opportunity sits outside the Summary Compensation Table.

notable_language.quote: The stretch PSUs are granted with performance goals that are designed to be extremely challenging in order to receive any vested shares. Given the attainment of the goals was not deemed probable as of the date of grant, there is no grant date fair value associated with these awards for accounting purposes

value.why_notable: Direct acknowledgment of a sharp stock decline juxtaposed with operating outperformance, used to defend the pay outcome.

notable_language.quote: Despite exceeding plan on targets for adjusted revenue and AOI, our cumulative TSR for the one- and three-year period ending December 31, 2025 was -35.1% and +2.3%, respectively. In line with our pay for performance philosophy, payouts under our long- and short-term incentive programs

value.why_notable: A large CEO salary increase framed as a neutral 'rebalancing' offset by a reduction in bonus target from 319% to 270% of salary.

notable_language.quote: For 2025, Kunal Kapoor’s salary increased 23.8% in connection with a rebalancing of his cash compensation to enhance competitiveness of his pay versus market data and with consideration to his salary remaining flat in 2024.

value.why_notable: Recurring justification for the Executive Chairman's $100,000 salary unchanged since 2000 and non-participation in incentive plans.

notable_language.quote: In consideration of his status as our principal shareholder, Joe believes that his compensation should be directly aligned with other shareholders and be realized primarily through appreciation in the long-term value of our common stock.

value.why_notable: New formal severance policy adopted in the same year the Chief Revenue Officer departed and forfeited his bonus and equity.

notable_language.quote: In May 2025, with input from our independent compensation consultant, we adopted the Morningstar, Inc. Executive Severance Policy (“Severance Policy”) for our NEOs (excluding Joe Mansueto) and certain other members of the executive leadership team to provide a uniform baseline and process for future executive departures and to align with market practices.

value.why_notable: Extended defense of the founder's share pledge, expanded in 2026 for a soccer stadium project — a recurring governance justification.

notable_language.quote: After examining these factors, the Audit Committee was satisfied that Joe possesses sufficient assets aside from his pledged Company shares to satisfy, if necessary, his indebtedness secured by those shares.

value.why_notable: Sets a deliberately measured tone against AI hype while still claiming positioning to benefit.

notable_language.quote: As always, we view such developments with interest—but also with patience and a long-term perspective. Our focus remains on building a business that compounds value over time.

value.why_notable: Core thesis statement framing the moat argument for an AI era.

notable_language.quote: We expect AI models will become ubiquitous and cheap, while high-quality, structured, and verifiable data backed by human insight will become even more valuable.

value.why_notable: Explicit self-description of the competitive moat as a compounding system — likely recurring framing.

notable_language.quote: More broadly, we believe our moat is not a single asset or technology. It is a compounding system in which data fuels research, research powers IP, and software and AI-enabled tools further embed us into our clients’ workflows.

value.why_notable: Unusually direct admission of share-price decline, reframed as a buyback opportunity.

notable_language.quote: While it has been painful to see the decline in our market value in 2025 and into 2026, it has also created an opportunity to increase our ownership in a business that we know as well as any and to deploy capital with high conviction.

value.why_notable: Rare acknowledgment of a weak spot: flat license growth in a flagship product.

notable_language.quote: We faced headwinds in Morningstar Direct, where license growth has been flat, although that area did contribute to growth, supported by increased revenue per license and expansion with existing clients in our reporting solutions business.

value.why_notable: Blunt aside signaling internal pressure on the research workforce in an AI environment.

notable_language.quote: Make no mistake, though: Our analysts know that they need to con- stantly up their game to deliver essential insights.

value.why_notable: Uses independence/criticism of clients' products as a branding claim.
